title: Forms
meta: Submit lab orders and maintain form definitions
intro: Forms lets staff enter data through published forms. Form authors use the builder to choose fields, preview the design and publish versions.

Use your own patients, enabled catalog tests and approved form design. The pictures show fictional records and an Example request form in an isolated test installation. No documentation samples are required.

Use forms allows reading form definitions. Submit forms allows data capture. Edit forms allows design changes, and Publish forms allows publication. A form also needs a valid submission configuration and an enabled workflow for incoming data before it can write data.
Draft and Archived forms can still open through View/Run. Submit is disabled until the form is Published. Preview in the builder is a separate way to try a design without saving a response.

The version numbers in these pictures are examples. Each publication saves a snapshot of the design and takes the next number. Your numbers depend on your own publication history. Read Start here for installation and command-line setup.

tasks.title: Choose the patient, test and specimen for a lab order
intro: Use this when recording an intended order through your published Lab order form. Use the patient and tests appropriate to that order.
steps: Open the Lab order row dots and select View/Run.
In Patient, search using your patient name or identifier.
Check the matching record and select the correct patient.
In Tests, search for the requested catalog test. The list uses tests switched on at this lab.
Select the requested test. Repeat this choice only when the order needs another test.
Under Results, select the chosen test row to open its details.
Select the specimen type recorded for this test. Use an option from your configured list.
tasks.result: The test details hold the chosen specimen. You have not submitted the order yet.

tasks.title: Review and submit the lab order
intro: Use this after selecting the patient, requested tests and specimen details. Complete any other required fields in your form before submitting.
steps: Select Close at the top right of the test-details sheet.
Choose the recorded Priority. The picture uses Routine.
Review the order and open its actions
Check the patient, tests and specimen details, then open the page dots at the top right.
Select Submit once. Wait for the result. Do not submit again merely to confirm success.
tasks.result: Response captured. confirms the saved response. The answers remain on screen. Another Submit is another write, so use it only for an intended submission.

tasks.title: Start a request-form design
intro: Use this when an existing form does not collect the information your workflow needs. The builder selects a FHIR healthcare data format and a record type.
steps: From Forms, open the page dots at the top right and select New.
Enter a name that describes its task. The example uses Example request form.
Open FHIR Version and choose the version your records require. The example selects R4 (most common).
Open Resource Type, find ServiceRequest and select it for this request-form example.
tasks.result: The available starter pack opens so you can choose its fields.

tasks.title: Choose starter-pack fields and save a draft
intro: Use the starter pack to keep the fields your form needs. This example keeps Patient, Tests, Results, Priority and Reference Number. Your own workflow may need more fields.
steps: Clear Requesting Clinician for this example
Clear Requesting Clinician when this example form does not collect it.
Clear Clinical Notes for this example
Clear Clinical Notes. Keep it selected in your own form if that workflow needs it.
Clear Referring Facility for this example
Clear Referring Facility for the five-field example.
Clear Order rejection for this example
Check that Patient, Tests, Results, Priority and Reference Number remain selected. The pictured pack shows 5 of 9 selected.
Open the starter-pack dots and select Add 5 fields.
Open the builder dots at the top right and select Save draft.
tasks.result: The form definition is saved as a Draft. Saving the design does not submit a response or publish it.

tasks.title: Change the reference-field wording
intro: Use this when the form should use wording staff recognise. This example changes Reference Number to Requisition reference.
steps: Select the Reference Number field's Edit control in the builder.
In Placeholder, enter Enter the requisition number. This hint appears inside an empty input.
Leave Required off when this answer is optional. Turn it on only when your workflow requires an answer.
Keep Enabled on so the field appears and collects an answer.
Open the field-editor dots and select Save. This applies the edit to the current builder design.
tasks.result: The field list shows Requisition reference. Use the builder's Save draft or Publish action to store the changed form.

tasks.title: Try the design without capturing data
intro: Use Preview to inspect the current builder design before publication. Its example answers do not become submitted form responses.
steps: Open the builder dots and select Preview.
Select the dots in the Preview sheet header.
Check the wording, fields and example answers. The example shows the Requisition reference input.
Open Preview actions again and select Reset.
Select Close at the top right to return to the builder.
tasks.result: You return to the same design. Fill example and Reset did not submit a response or save the form definition.

tasks.title: Save and publish the reviewed design
intro: Use this when the design is ready for use. Publishing stores the current design and creates a numbered snapshot.
steps: Open the builder dots and select Save draft.
Open the builder dots again and select Publish.
Check the published status and generated snapshot number in the header. You cannot type this number.
tasks.result: The Forms list shows the form as Published. Submission still requires valid answers and a configured capture workflow.

tasks.title: Compare a changed placeholder with a published version
intro: Use this before publishing a later change. The example changes only the reference-field placeholder; its label already matches the published version.
steps: Open the Requisition reference field editor. Change Placeholder to Enter the reference from the paper form, then use the field dots to Save.
Open the builder dots and select Compare.
Open the left selector and choose the published snapshot to compare. The example selects v1.
Keep Current draft in the right selector to compare the design presently in the builder. You can also choose another published version.
The example reports one changed field property, Field reference-number · placeholder. It does not report a label change.
Press Escape to return to the builder. Closing Compare does not save or publish the changed design.
tasks.result: You have reviewed the difference while retaining the current builder edit.

tasks.title: Save and publish a later content change
intro: Use this after reviewing a change against a published version.
steps: Open the builder dots and select Save draft.
When saved content differs from the published content, the current form becomes Draft. View/Run can still open it, but Submit is disabled until publication.
Open the builder dots and select Publish when the change is ready.
tasks.result: The form becomes Published with the next snapshot number. An unchanged save does not by itself turn a Published form into Draft.

tasks.title: Restore the content of a published snapshot
intro: Use this when an earlier published design contains the content you want. Restoring replaces the editable form with that snapshot.
steps: Open the builder dots and select Versions.
Read its version number, label and publication date. The list puts newest versions first and has pagination when needed.
Select the dots on the snapshot you want to restore. The picture uses version 1.
Read the confirmation, then select Restore to replace the current design. Cancel keeps the current design.
The pictured restore changes the published content, so the form becomes Draft. Restoring identical content can leave a Published form Published.
tasks.result: The builder contains the restored content. A restored Draft remains viewable through View/Run, with Submit disabled until it is published.

tasks.title: Publish reviewed restored content
intro: Use this after checking that restored Draft content is the design you want staff to use.
steps: Open the builder dots and select Publish.
Read the published version in the header. Republishing creates the next snapshot; it does not reuse the restored snapshot number.
tasks.result: The restored design is Published again. The example installation has snapshots 1 through 4; those numbers are illustrative.

tasks.title: Export the form definition
intro: Use this when you need the form as a FHIR Questionnaire JSON file. This export contains the definition, not submitted answers.
steps: Return to Forms and open the dots on the form you want to export.
Select Export. Your browser downloads the Questionnaire JSON file.
tasks.result: The downloaded file contains the form definition. Export does not submit or change the form.

tasks.title: Make a separate draft and inspect its submission state
intro: Use Duplicate when you want to adapt an existing form while retaining its original definition.
steps: From the original form row dots, select Duplicate.
Find the new copy in Forms. It starts as a Draft. The original form remains.
Open the copy's row dots and select View/Run. The page warns that submission is disabled until publication.
Open the page dots. Submit is disabled on this unpublished form.
tasks.result: The copy remains a separate Draft. Opening View/Run does not publish it or submit answers.

tasks.title: Archive or delete an unused copy
intro: Use Archive to retain a definition while stopping submission use. Delete permanently removes the chosen definition. The pictures retire only the separate demonstration copy.
steps: Select Forms in the main menu. Find the copy you intend to retire.
Open its row dots and select Archive.
The copy remains in the management list with Archived status. It is no longer Published for submission.
Choose Delete when removal is intended
If you intend permanent removal, open that same copy's row dots and select Delete. Check that you chose the copy, not the original.
Read the form name in the confirmation. Select Delete to remove it, or Cancel to keep it.
tasks.result: The deleted copy disappears from Forms. The captured example retained its original form.

tasks.title: Inspect forms and previews on a phone
intro: Use the same Forms list and builder actions on a phone. A wide table can scroll horizontally.
steps: Use Search forms in the phone-width list.
Open the form in the builder and select its dots at the top right.
Read the preview and scroll its fields. Preview actions remains in its header dots.
tasks.result: The design remains available for inspection at phone width.

end.title: Limits
paragraphs: This walkthrough captures an order and specimen choice. It does not demonstrate entering laboratory result values or rejecting an order.
Field-editor Save applies a local builder edit. Builder Save draft stores the definition. Publish stores the design and creates a version. Preview actions do none of these writes.
Saving or restoring different content can return a Published form to Draft. Identical content does not force that change. View/Run remains available, but submission requires Published status.

end.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: No patient matches. Check the search value and whether your normal feed has supplied that patient. Use Patients to inspect the received record.
A test is absent. Check that it exists in Test catalog and is switched on at this lab.
Submit is disabled. Check the form status and submission-readiness message. Publish a reviewed Draft and check the capture configuration.
Submit reports invalid answers. Read the field errors and correct required or invalid values before retrying. A successful Response captured message does not need a second submission.
Restore leaves Draft. Review the restored content, then Publish it when it should be available for submission again.

end.title: Related guides
paragraphs: Read Patients for received patient records and Test catalog for lab-enabled tests. Read Workflows for the capture workflow and Start here for installation and command-line setup.

end.title: Optional practice
paragraphs: Use a test installation with fictional patients and lab-enabled test definitions. The capture tasks work with your own received records; no documentation sample file is required.

For design practice, use a separate form name and the five-field ServiceRequest example. Try Preview, Save draft, Publish, Compare and Versions. Duplicate that definition before practising Archive or Delete.
Submit a test Lab order only when you intend to write that order. The documented example submitted one response. Its later screenshots did not submit another response.
